examples.english: All workers on the morning [shift] get a free breakfast.
examples.chinese: 所有早[班]的工人都能得到一份免费早餐。

examples.english: My dad usually goes to bed early before his early [shift].
examples.chinese: 我爸爸上早[班]前通常会早早睡觉。

meanings.explanation: If you [shift] something, you move it from one place, position, or direction to another.

examples.english: Can you [shift] your chair a little closer to the table?
examples.chinese: 你能把椅子[挪]得离桌子近一点吗？

examples.english: I [shifted] my bike from the hallway to the balcony this morning.
examples.chinese: 我今天早上把自行车从走廊[移]到了阳台。

examples.english: She often [shifts] her desk around her room.
examples.chinese: 她经常[挪动]房间里的书桌。

meanings.explanation: A [signal] is a gesture, sound, or object that gives someone information, a warning, or an instruction.

examples.english: The red light is a [signal] to stop.
examples.chinese: 红灯是停下来的[信号]。

examples.english: She gave me a [signal] to be quiet.
examples.chinese: 她给我一个保持安静的[暗号]。

examples.english: The teacher raised her hand as a [signal] for us to line up.
examples.chinese: 老师举手作为让我们排队的[信号]。

meanings.explanation: If you [signal] to someone, you make a gesture or sound to send them a message or tell them to do something.

examples.english: He [signaled] to me to come over.
examples.chinese: 他[示意]我过去。

examples.english: The bell [signals] the end of class.
examples.chinese: 铃声[表示]下课了。

examples.english: She [signaled] the waiter by raising her hand.
examples.chinese: 她举手向服务员[示意]。

meanings.explanation: If you [stretch] something, you pull it so that it becomes longer or bigger, and if it stretches, it becomes longer or bigger when pulled.

examples.english: I [stretched] the rubber band and it broke.
examples.chinese: 我把橡皮筋[拉]断了。

examples.english: The sweater [stretched] after I washed it.
examples.chinese: 这件毛衣洗过之后[变大]了。

examples.english: You can [stretch] this hat to fit your head.
examples.chinese: 你可以把这顶帽子[撑大]来适配你的头。

meanings.explanation: When you [stretch], you straighten or move your arms, legs, or body to its full length, especially to make yourself more comfortable or to reach something.

examples.english: I like to [stretch] my legs after sitting for a long time.
examples.chinese: 坐了很久之后我喜欢[伸伸]腿。

examples.english: She [stretched] her arms above her head.
examples.chinese: 她把胳膊[举过头顶伸了伸]。

examples.english: Wake up and [stretch] your body every morning.
examples.chinese: 每天早上醒来[伸懒腰]。

meanings.explanation: A [stretch] of something is a continuous area of land, water, or time.

examples.english: We drove along a beautiful [stretch] of beach.
examples.chinese: 我们沿着美不胜收的[一段]海滩开车。

examples.english: This is the hardest [stretch] of the race.
examples.chinese: 这是比赛中最艰难的[一段]。

examples.english: I studied for hours on end, working for long [stretches].
examples.chinese: 我连续学习了好几个小时，长时间[不间断]地用功。

meanings.explanation: The [structure] of something is the way in which it is made, built, or organized.

examples.english: The [structure] of this bridge is very strong.
examples.chinese: 这座桥的[结构]非常坚固。

examples.english: A good story needs a clear [structure] with a beginning, middle, and end.
examples.chinese: 一个好故事需要有清晰的[结构]，包括开头、中间和结尾。

examples.english: The [structure] of this school building is modern and safe.
examples.chinese: 这所学校的[建筑结构]既现代又安全。

meanings.explanation: To [structure] something means to arrange or organize it in a particular way.

examples.english: You need to [structure] your essay before you start writing.
examples.chinese: 你开始写作之前，需要先[规划]好文章的结构。

examples.english: The teacher taught us how to [structure] a good paragraph.
examples.chinese: 老师教我们如何[组织]好一个段落。

examples.english: We should [structure] our day to finish homework on time.
examples.chinese: 我们应该[安排]好一天的时间，按时完成作业。

meanings.explanation: A [series] of things or events is a number of similar things that happen one after another or are connected with each other.

examples.english: I read a whole [series] of comic books during the holiday.
examples.chinese: 假期里我读了一整[系列]漫画书。

examples.english: The museum showed a [series] of famous paintings.
examples.chinese: 博物馆展出了一[系列]名画。

examples.english: We solved a [series] of puzzles in class.
examples.chinese: 我们在课堂上解决了一[系列]谜题。

meanings.explanation: A television or radio [series] is a set of programs of the same kind that are broadcast regularly.

examples.english: I watch my favorite TV [series] every Saturday night.
examples.chinese: 我每周六晚都看我最喜欢的电视[系列片]。

examples.english: A new cartoon [series] starts next week.
examples.chinese: 下周将播出一部新的动画[系列片]。

examples.english: This [series] has ten episodes.
examples.chinese: 这部[系列剧]有十集。

meanings.explanation: A [society] is the entire community of people who live together in an organized group, sharing laws, customs, and ways of life.

examples.english: Everyone should help make [society] a better place.
examples.chinese: 每个人都应该帮助让[社会]变得更美好。

examples.english: New technology changes how [society] works.
examples.chinese: 新技术改变了[社会]的运转方式。

examples.english: We learn how to get along with others in [society].
examples.chinese: 我们学习如何在[社会]中和他人相处。

meanings.explanation: A [society] is an organized group of people who share the same hobby, interest, or goal.

examples.english: My mom joined a gardening [society] last year.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈去年加入了一个园艺[协会]。

examples.english: This [society] helps protect wild animals.
examples.chinese: 这个[协会]帮助保护野生动物。

examples.english: I want to join the photography [society] at school.
examples.chinese: 我想加入学校的摄影[协会]。

meanings.explanation: A [thief] is a person who steals things from other people, especially secretly and without using violence.

examples.english: A [thief] stole my mom's bag at the supermarket.
examples.chinese: 一个[小偷]在超市偷了我妈的包。

examples.english: The police caught the [thief] and took him away.
examples.chinese: 警察抓住了那个[小偷]，把他带走了。

examples.english: Don't leave your phone on the table, or a [thief] might take it.
examples.chinese: 别把手机放在桌上，不然[小偷]会把它拿走。

meanings.explanation: [Technology] refers to the use of scientific knowledge and tools to create machines, devices, and systems that help people do things more easily or solve problems.

examples.english: Smartphones are a kind of [technology] that helps us talk to friends far away.
examples.chinese: 智能手机是一种[科技]，能帮助我们跟远方的朋友通话。

examples.english: My school uses new [technology] to make learning more fun.
examples.chinese: 我的学校使用新[科技]让学习更有趣。

examples.english: Doctors use [technology] to find out why people feel sick.
examples.chinese: 医生用[科技]来查清楚人们为什么生病。

meanings.explanation: [Technology] can also mean a particular method, skill, or way of doing something that uses special tools or knowledge.

examples.english: Ancient people used simple [technology] like wheels to move heavy things.
examples.chinese: 古人使用像轮子这样简单的[技术]来搬运重物。

examples.english: This car factory has the latest [technology] for making electric cars.
examples.chinese: 这家汽车工厂拥有制造电动汽车的最新[技术]。

examples.english: Farmers today use [technology] to grow more food with less water.
examples.chinese: 如今的农民用[技术]来用更少的水种出更多粮食。

meanings.explanation: If you describe something as [unforgettable], you mean that it is extremely good, interesting, or beautiful and you cannot forget it.

examples.english: Our trip to the beach was truly [unforgettable].
examples.chinese: 我们的海边之旅真的[令人难忘]。

examples.english: My grandmother told me an [unforgettable] story last night.
examples.chinese: 奶奶昨晚给我讲了一个[难忘的]故事。

examples.english: It was an [unforgettable] day when I met my best friend.
examples.chinese: 遇见我最好朋友的那天是[难忘]的一天。

meanings.explanation: A [wonderland] is a place that is beautiful, magical, and full of wonderful things. It often refers to a place that feels like something out of a fairy tale or a dream.

examples.english: After the snow, our town looked like a beautiful [wonderland].
examples.chinese: 下雪之后，我们的小镇就像一个美丽的[仙境]。

examples.english: The theme park is a [wonderland] for kids.
examples.chinese: 这个主题公园是孩子们的[乐园]。

examples.english: She opened the old book and stepped into a [wonderland] of stories.
examples.chinese: 她翻开那本旧书，走进了一个故事的[奇幻世界]。

meanings.explanation: A [train] is a railway vehicle that carries passengers or goods from one place to another.

examples.english: I take the [train] to school every day.
examples.chinese: 我每天坐[火车]去学校。

examples.english: The [train] arrived at the station on time.
examples.chinese: [火车]准时到达了车站。

examples.english: We caught the last [train] home.
examples.chinese: 我们赶上了回家的最后一班[火车]。

meanings.explanation: To [train] means to teach someone to do something or to prepare yourself for something through practice.

examples.english: My coach helps me [train] for the soccer game.
examples.chinese: 教练帮我[训练]足球比赛。

examples.english: She wants to [train] her dog to sit.
examples.chinese: 她想[训练]她的狗坐下。

examples.english: He [train]s to be a doctor at the university.
examples.chinese: 他在大学[学习]成为一名医生。

meanings.explanation: A [tsunami] is a very large ocean wave, usually caused by an earthquake under the sea, that can cause great damage when it reaches land.

examples.english: The big [tsunami] washed away many houses by the sea.
examples.chinese: 大[海啸]把海边的好多房子都冲走了。

examples.english: Everyone ran to high hills when the [tsunami] came.
examples.chinese: [海啸]来的时候，大家都跑到了高山上。

examples.english: We learned what to do if a [tsunami] happens.
examples.chinese: 我们学到了[海啸]来了该怎么办。

meanings.explanation: If you talk about a [specific] thing or person, you are referring to one particular thing or person, rather than a general one.

examples.english: We need to find a [specific] book about dinosaurs for our project.
examples.chinese: 我们需要找一本[特定]的关于恐龙的书来做项目。

examples.english: Each student in the class has a [specific] job to do.
examples.chinese: 班上的每个学生都有自己[特定]的任务要做。

examples.english: Please tell me the [specific] time when the party starts.
examples.chinese: 请告诉我派对开始的[具体]时间。

meanings.explanation: If you are [specific], you give clear, exact, and detailed information about something, rather than being vague.

examples.english: Can you be more [specific] about what you want for your birthday?
examples.chinese: 你能更[具体]地说说你生日想要什么吗？

examples.english: The teacher gave us very [specific] instructions for the homework.
examples.chinese: 老师给了我们非常[明确]的家庭作业说明。

examples.english: My mom was very [specific] about the rules for using the computer.
examples.chinese: 妈妈对用电脑的规矩说得很[清楚]。

meanings.explanation: A [system] is a group of related parts that work together as a whole.

examples.english: The solar [system] has eight planets that go around the sun.
examples.chinese: 太阳[系]里有八颗行星绕着太阳转。

examples.english: We have a heating [system] in our house that keeps us warm in winter.
examples.chinese: 我们家有暖气[系统]，冬天特别暖和。

examples.english: Your body has a digestive [system] that helps you break down food.
examples.chinese: 你的身体有消化[系统]，帮你消化食物。

meanings.explanation: A [system] is a particular way of doing something that follows a fixed plan or set of rules.

examples.english: Our school has a [system] for borrowing books from the library.
examples.chinese: 我们学校有从图书馆借书的[制度]。

examples.english: She created a [system] to organize her toys by color.
examples.chinese: 她想了个[办法]，按颜色把玩具整理好。

examples.english: We need a better [system] for taking turns on the swings.
examples.chinese: 我们得想个更好的[办法]来轮流荡秋千。

meanings.explanation: If you [strike] someone or something, you hit them with your hand or with an object.

examples.english: He [struck] the drum with a stick.
examples.chinese: 他用棍子[敲打]鼓。

examples.english: Lightning [struck] the tall tree last night.
examples.chinese: 昨晚闪电[击中]了那棵大树。

examples.english: The cat [struck] the toy ball with its paw.
examples.chinese: 猫用爪子[拍打]玩具球。

meanings.explanation: A [strike] is a period of time when a group of workers stop working because they want more money or better working conditions.

examples.english: The bus drivers went on [strike] for better pay.
examples.chinese: 公交车司机为了涨工资[罢工]了。

examples.english: There was a [strike] at the factory last month.
examples.chinese: 上个月工厂发生了[罢工]。

examples.english: The teachers are on [strike] today.
examples.chinese: 老师们今天[罢工]。

meanings.explanation: [Therapy] is the treatment of a physical illness, injury, or health problem, often using methods other than drugs or surgery.

examples.english: My grandma goes to [therapy] every week for her sore back.
examples.chinese: 我奶奶因为腰背酸痛每周都去做[治疗]。

examples.english: He does leg [therapy] after breaking his leg last month.
examples.chinese: 他上个月摔断腿后，现在做腿部[治疗]。

examples.english: My aunt goes to weekly [therapy] to help her feel less sad.
examples.chinese: 我阿姨每周去做[治疗]来缓解低落的情绪。

meanings.explanation: [Therapy] refers to the process of talking to a trained professional to improve mental or emotional problems.

examples.english: After her dog died, my neighbor started going to [therapy].
examples.chinese: 邻居家的狗狗去世后，她开始去做[心理治疗]。

examples.english: My mom's friend goes to [therapy] every Friday to talk about her feelings.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈的朋友每个星期五都去做[心理治疗]，倾诉她的情绪。

examples.english: Many kids find [therapy] helps them when they feel very scared or sad.
examples.chinese: 很多孩子发现，当他们感到恐惧或悲伤时，[心理治疗]很有帮助。

meanings.explanation: An [unidentified] person or thing has not had its identity or nature discovered or recognized.

examples.english: An [unidentified] cat walked into our classroom today.
examples.chinese: 一只[来历不明的]猫今天走进了我们教室。

examples.english: My dad saw an [unidentified] truck parked near our house.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸看见一辆[身份不明的]卡车停在我家附近。

examples.english: Children saw an [unidentified] object flying in the sky yesterday.
examples.chinese: 孩子们昨天看见一个[不明]物体在空中飞行。

meanings.explanation: A [wound] is an injury to part of your body, especially one that is made by a cut or a hole in your skin.

examples.english: The boy fell off his bike and got a [wound] on his knee.
examples.chinese: 那个男孩从自行车上摔下来，膝盖上受了[伤]。

examples.english: The doctor cleaned the [wound] and put a bandage on it.
examples.chinese: 医生清理了[伤口]并贴上了创可贴。

examples.english: Her [wound] healed quickly because she took good care of it.
examples.chinese: 她的[伤口]很快就愈合了，因为她护理得很仔细。

meanings.explanation: To [wound] someone means to hurt their body by making a cut or hole in their skin, or to hurt their feelings.

examples.english: The broken glass [wounded] his hand.
examples.chinese: 碎玻璃[弄伤]了他的手。

examples.english: His unkind words [wounded] her feelings.
examples.chinese: 他那些不友善的话[伤害]了她的感情。

examples.english: Be careful not to [wound] yourself with that sharp knife.
examples.chinese: 小心别被那把锋利的刀[弄伤]了自己。

meanings.explanation: A [chance] is an opportunity to do something or a possibility that something will happen.

examples.english: This is your last [chance] to win the game.
examples.chinese: 这是你赢下比赛的最后[机会]。

examples.english: I hope I have a [chance] to visit Beijing someday.
examples.chinese: 希望有一天我能有[机会]去北京看看。

examples.english: There is a small [chance] of rain tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 明天有很小的[可能]会下雨。

meanings.explanation: [Feedback] is advice, opinions, or comments about how well someone is doing something, which are intended to help them improve.

examples.english: The teacher gave me some useful [feedback] on my essay.
examples.chinese: 老师就我的作文给我提了一些有用的[反馈意见]。

examples.english: We always ask our customers for [feedback] after they buy something.
examples.chinese: 顾客买东西之后，我们总会请他们提供[反馈]。

examples.english: Your [feedback] will help us make the app better.
examples.chinese: 你的[反馈]会帮助我们把这个应用做得更好。

meanings.explanation: A [craze] is an activity, style, or interest that suddenly becomes very popular for a short period of time.

examples.english: There was a big [craze] for collecting stickers at my school.
examples.chinese: 我们学校曾刮起一股收集贴纸的[热潮]。

examples.english: The new dance became a [craze] among young people.
examples.chinese: 这种新舞蹈在年轻人中成了一阵[风潮]。

examples.english: Last year's toy [craze] has finally died down.
examples.chinese: 去年的玩具[热潮]终于平息了。

meanings.explanation: [Culture] is the customs, beliefs, ideas, and way of life of a particular group of people or society.

examples.english: Chinese people often drink tea, and this is part of Chinese [culture].
examples.chinese: 中国人经常喝茶，这是中国[文化]的一部分。

examples.english: Learning about different [cultures] helps us understand the world better.
examples.chinese: 了解不同的[文化]有助于我们更好地认识世界。

examples.english: Every country has its own food [culture].
examples.chinese: 每个国家都有自己的饮食[文化]。

meanings.explanation: [Culture] also refers to art, music, literature, and other activities that show a society's artistic and intellectual achievements.

examples.english: The city is famous for its rich [culture], with many theaters and museums.
examples.chinese: 这座城市以丰富的[文化]闻名，有很多剧院和博物馆。

examples.english: My mom loves [culture], so she goes to see art shows every weekend.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈很热爱[文化]，每个周末都去看艺术展览。

examples.english: Music and painting are important parts of a country's [culture].
examples.chinese: 音乐和绘画是一个国家[文化]的重要组成部分。

meanings.explanation: An [agency] is a business or organization that provides a particular service to people or other groups.

examples.english: My family booked our summer hotel through a travel [agency].
examples.chinese: 我们一家通过一家旅行[代理机构]预订了暑期酒店。

examples.english: This [agency] helps people find good jobs near their homes.
examples.chinese: 这家[中介机构]帮人们找到家附近的好工作。

examples.english: My aunt works for a government [agency] that protects wild animals.
examples.chinese: 我阿姨在一家保护野生动物的政府[机构]工作。

meanings.explanation: [Agency] is the ability of a person to act independently and make their own decisions to achieve what they want.

examples.english: Kids should have some [agency] when picking what to eat for lunch.
examples.chinese: 孩子们选午餐吃什么的时候应该有一些[自主权]。

examples.english: My teacher gave us more [agency] to plan our end-of-term class party.
examples.chinese: 我的老师给了我们更多[自主权]来策划期末班级派对。

examples.english: Having [agency] means you can make your own choices instead of always following others.
examples.chinese: 拥有[自主权]意味着你可以自己做选择，而不是一直听从他人。

meanings.explanation: [Interstellar] describes things that exist or happen between the stars in outer space.

examples.english: Scientists are still studying [interstellar] space.
examples.chinese: 科学家们仍在研究[星际]空间。

examples.english: Many science fiction stories talk about [interstellar] travel.
examples.chinese: 许多科幻故事都讲到了[星际]旅行。

examples.english: Some movies are about exciting [interstellar] adventures.
examples.chinese: 有些电影讲述了激动人心的[星际]冒险。

meanings.explanation: If you [compare] two or more things, you look at them carefully to see how they are similar and how they are different.

examples.english: Let's [compare] the two apples to see which is sweeter.
examples.chinese: 我们来[比较]一下这两个苹果，看看哪个更甜。

examples.english: My mom always [compares] prices before she buys clothes.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈买衣服前总会[比较]价格。

examples.english: After finishing homework, we can [compare] answers with each other.
examples.chinese: 做完作业后，我们可以互相[比对]一下答案。

meanings.explanation: If you [compare] one thing to another, you say that the first thing is similar to the second thing, often to help others understand it better.

examples.english: The writer [compared] the moon to a silver plate.
examples.chinese: 作家把月亮[比作]一个银盘子。

examples.english: People often [compare] books to good friends.
examples.chinese: 人们常把书[比作]好朋友。

examples.english: He [compared] running to a kind of medicine for bad moods.
examples.chinese: 他把跑步[比作]治疗坏情绪的良药。

meanings.explanation: If you say something is [overall], you mean including all the things or parts; total or general.

examples.english: My [overall] score in the math test is 95.
examples.chinese: 我数学考试[总分]是95分。

examples.english: The [overall] design of this park is very beautiful.
examples.chinese: 这座公园的[整体]设计很漂亮。

examples.english: What's the [overall] cost of the birthday party?
examples.chinese: 生日聚会的[总]费用是多少？

meanings.explanation: If you say [overall], you mean in general, considering everything together; on the whole.

examples.english: [Overall], I think this movie is very interesting.
examples.chinese: [总的来说]，我觉得这部电影很有趣。

examples.english: [Overall], our school trip was great fun.
examples.chinese: [总体来说]，我们学校的这次旅行非常开心。

examples.english: My sister did [overall] well in her exams this year.
examples.chinese: 我姐姐今年考试[总体上]考得不错。

meanings.explanation: If you [deserve] something, you have earned it or are worthy of it because of your actions, qualities, or the way you have been treated.

examples.english: After helping grandma clean the house, you [deserve] an ice cream.
examples.chinese: 帮奶奶打扫完房子，你[值得]一个冰淇淋。

examples.english: Our team [deserves] to win the game today.
examples.chinese: 我们队今天[值得]赢得这场比赛。

examples.english: He [deserves] punishment for lying to his teacher.
examples.chinese: 他对老师撒谎，[值得]受到惩罚。

meanings.explanation: A [champion] is a person or team that has won a competition or game.

examples.english: She won the race and became the school [champion].
examples.chinese: 她赢了赛跑，成了学校的[冠军]。

examples.english: Our soccer team are the [champions] this year.
examples.chinese: 我们足球队今年是[冠军]。

examples.english: He trained hard to become a [champion].
examples.chinese: 他努力训练想成为[冠军]。

meanings.explanation: [Evidence] is any fact, object, or sign that makes you believe that something is true or really happened.

examples.english: Mom found [evidence] that someone had eaten the cookies.
examples.chinese: 妈妈找到了[证据]，证明有人偷吃了饼干。

examples.english: The footprints in the mud were [evidence] that a deer had been in the garden.
examples.chinese: 泥地上的脚印就是鹿来过花园的[证据]。

examples.english: There is no [evidence] that the dog opened the door by itself.
examples.chinese: 没有[证据]表明狗是自己打开门的。

meanings.explanation: A [relative] is a member of your family, such as an aunt, uncle, or cousin.

examples.english: We visited my [relative] in the countryside last weekend.
examples.chinese: 上周末我们去乡下看望了我的[亲戚]。

examples.english: My grandma has many [relatives] living in different cities.
examples.chinese: 我奶奶有很多[亲戚]住在不同的城市。

examples.english: During the Spring Festival, all my [relatives] come to our house for dinner.
examples.chinese: 春节的时候，所有的[亲戚]都来我家吃年夜饭。

meanings.explanation: If something is [relative], it means it is being considered in relation to something else, rather than being absolute or fixed.

examples.english: This question is [relatively] easy compared to the last one.
examples.chinese: 跟上一题比，这道题[相对来说]简单一些。

examples.english: The price of this toy is high, but it's [relatively] cheap for its quality.
examples.chinese: 这个玩具的价格挺高的，但跟它的质量比[算比较便宜的了]。

examples.english: Is success [relative]? Different people have different ideas.
examples.chinese: 成功是不是[相对的]呢？不同的人有不同的看法。

meanings.explanation: A [province] is a large area that is part of a country, often with its own local government.

examples.english: My family lives in a [province] called Fujian.
examples.chinese: 我家住在一个叫福建的[省]。

examples.english: Canada is divided into ten [provinces] and three territories.
examples.chinese: 加拿大分为十个[省]和三个地区。

examples.english: We studied the map of each [province] in geography class yesterday.
examples.chinese: 昨天地理课上我们看了每个[省]的地图。

meanings.explanation: A [workout] is a period of physical exercise that you do to keep fit or stay healthy.

examples.english: I go to the gym for a [workout] every morning.
examples.chinese: 我每天早上都去健身房[锻炼]。

examples.english: That was a really hard [workout]!
examples.chinese: 那次[锻炼]真是累死了！

examples.english: She does a 30-minute [workout] before school.
examples.chinese: 她上学前会做30分钟的[锻炼]。

meanings.explanation: If you [steal] something, you take it without asking the owner and without planning to give it back.

examples.english: Someone [stole] my bike from the park.
examples.chinese: 有人在公园里把我的自行车[偷]走了。

examples.english: He got caught trying to [steal] a candy bar from the shop.
examples.chinese: 他想从店里[偷]一块巧克力棒，结果被抓住了。

examples.english: Don't ever [steal] other people's things.
examples.chinese: 千万不要[偷]别人的东西。

meanings.explanation: If something is a [steal], it is sold at a very low price, making it a great bargain.

examples.english: This jacket is only ten dollars — what a [steal]!
examples.chinese: 这件外套才十美元，简直太[划算]了！

examples.english: I got this TV on sale for half price — it was a real [steal].
examples.chinese: 我半价买了这台电视，真[便宜]。

examples.english: At that price, it's an absolute [steal].
examples.chinese: 这个价格真是[捡到大便宜了]。

meanings.explanation: If a sharp object [pierces] something, it makes a hole in it or goes all the way through it.

examples.english: The needle [pierced] my finger when I was sewing.
examples.chinese: 我缝衣服的时候，针[扎破]了我的手指。

examples.english: My mom [pierced] a small hole in the paper with a pencil.
examples.chinese: 妈妈用铅笔在纸上[扎]了一个小洞。

examples.english: The arrow [pierced] the apple on the tree branch.
examples.chinese: 箭[射穿]了树枝上的苹果。

meanings.explanation: If a sound or light [pierces] through something, it cuts through it and becomes suddenly clear to hear or see.

examples.english: A scream [pierced] the quiet night.
examples.chinese: 一声尖叫[划破]了宁静的夜晚。

examples.english: Bright sunlight [pierced] the dark clouds after the rain.
examples.chinese: 雨后明媚的阳光[穿透]了乌云。

examples.english: The bird's clear song [pierced] through the quiet forest.
examples.chinese: 鸟儿清脆的歌声[穿过]了寂静的森林。

meanings.explanation: If something or someone [remains] in a particular state or place, they continue to be in that state or place.

examples.english: Only a few apples [remained] on the tree after the harvest.
examples.chinese: 收割后，树上只[剩下]几个苹果了。

examples.english: Please [remain] quiet when the baby is sleeping.
examples.chinese: 宝宝睡觉的时候，请[保持]安静。

examples.english: We [remained] friends after moving to different cities.
examples.chinese: 搬到不同城市后，我们依然[保持]着朋友关系。

meanings.explanation: If something [remains] to be done, it still needs to be dealt with or completed.

examples.english: Lots of homework [remains] to be done tonight.
examples.chinese: 今晚还有很多作业[有待]完成。

examples.english: Only one question [remains] to be answered.
examples.chinese: 只剩一个问题[有待]解答。

examples.english: Nothing [remains] to be added to this story.
examples.chinese: 这个故事已经没什么[需要]补充了。

meanings.explanation: If you [succeed], you achieve what you intended or wanted to achieve.

examples.english: My cousin [succeeded] in getting into his dream school.
examples.chinese: 我表哥[成功]考入了他梦想的学校。

examples.english: If you keep practicing, you will [succeed] one day.
examples.chinese: 如果你坚持练习，总有一天会[成功]的。

examples.english: She [succeeded] because she never gave up.
examples.chinese: 她之所以[成功]，是因为她从不放弃。

meanings.explanation: If you [succeed] someone in a position, you take their place after they leave.

examples.english: The prince [succeeded] his father as king.
examples.chinese: 王子[继承]父亲成为国王。

examples.english: She [succeeded] Mr. Smith as our new teacher.
examples.chinese: 她[接替]史密斯先生成为我们的新老师。

examples.english: He [succeeded] his uncle as the head of the company.
examples.chinese: 他[接任]他叔叔成为公司负责人。

meanings.explanation: The [solar system] is the sun and all the planets, moons, comets, and other objects that travel around it in space.

examples.english: There are eight planets in our [solar system].
examples.chinese: 我们的[太阳系]里有八颗行星。

examples.english: The Earth is part of the [solar system].
examples.chinese: 地球是[太阳系]的一部分。

examples.english: We learned about the [solar system] in science class today.
examples.chinese: 我们今天在科学课上学习了[太阳系]。

meanings.explanation: A [muscle] is a part of your body that tightens and relaxes to help you move. Your muscles help you run, jump, lift things, and keep your body strong.

examples.english: Swimming is a great way to build [muscle].
examples.chinese: 游泳是锻炼[肌肉]的好方法。

examples.english: I pulled a [muscle] in my back from lifting wrong.
examples.chinese: 我搬东西姿势不对，拉伤了背部的[肌肉]。

examples.english: Athletes have very strong [muscles] because they train every day.
examples.chinese: 运动员每天训练，所以[肌肉]非常强健。

meanings.explanation: If something [surrounds] a place or person, it is all around them on every side.

examples.english: Tall trees [surround] our house.
examples.chinese: 高大的树木[环绕]着我们的房子。

examples.english: The children [surrounded] their teacher on the playground.
examples.chinese: 孩子们在操场上[围住了]他们的老师。

examples.english: A high wall [surrounds] the old garden.
examples.chinese: 一堵高墙[环绕]着那个旧花园。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [swift] happens or moves very quickly.

examples.english: The cat made a [swift] jump and caught the ball.
examples.chinese: 猫[敏捷地]一跳，接住了球。

examples.english: Thank you for your [swift] reply to my email.
examples.chinese: 谢谢你这么[迅速地]回复我的邮件。

examples.english: The [swift] river carried the leaves away in no time.
examples.chinese: [湍急的]河水一下子就把树叶冲走了。

meanings.explanation: When you [digest] food, your body breaks it down into smaller parts that can be absorbed and used for energy and growth.

examples.english: It takes a few hours to [digest] a big, heavy meal.
examples.chinese: [消化]一顿丰盛油腻的大餐需要几个小时。

examples.english: My cat eats slowly to help her [digest] her food properly.
examples.chinese: 我的猫慢慢吃东西，帮自己更好地[消化]食物。

examples.english: Drinking warm water after a meal can help your body [digest] food.
examples.chinese: 饭后喝温水能帮助身体[消化]食物。

meanings.explanation: A [digest] is a short collection of summaries of articles, news, or stories, usually on a specific topic.

examples.english: The school puts out a monthly [digest] of students' best writing.
examples.chinese: 学校每月会出一本学生优秀习作的[文摘]。

examples.english: I read a [digest] of the week's top news every Sunday morning.
examples.chinese: 我每个周日早上都会读一周重要新闻的[摘要]。

examples.english: This children's science [digest] has many fun facts for kids my age.
examples.chinese: 这本少儿科学[文摘]有很多适合我这个年龄孩子的有趣知识。

meanings.explanation: A [prize] is something that is given to someone who wins a competition, race, or game, or as a reward for doing something very good.

examples.english: She won the first [prize] in the drawing competition.
examples.chinese: 她在绘画比赛中获得了一等[奖]。

examples.english: The [prize] for the winner was a big teddy bear.
examples.chinese: 获胜者的[奖品]是一只大泰迪熊。

examples.english: He shared his [prize] with his best friend.
examples.chinese: 他和最好的朋友分享了[奖品]。
